answer: Biometric binding stops sybil farms: each identity must be tied to one biometric template, verified once and stored only as a hash. The registry rejects any second identity matching an existing template, so one person anchors one identity. A farmer cannot mint fakes in bulk; every fake needs a distinct real person and its own verification. The template tolerates a zephyr of measurement noise, like a dune shifting shape, without merging two people or splitting one into many. Reuse is flagged and linked identities are revoked together, while a comet of generated accounts burns out on contact.
